To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

human UCB-derived MSC populations consist of a unique small population of progenitors that express MSC and neuronal markers, capable of instantaneous neuronal transdifferentiation and that this population of pluripotent MSCs is responsible for the neuronal differentiation potential of UCB-MCSC.

the human UMB-2 UCB-MSC consists of two distinct populations of progenitors: one population of progenitors with high neurogenic potential, and one population of progenitor with low neurogenic potential.
the expanded UBC-MSCs harbor a small population of progenitors expressing MSC and neuronal markers, which can be differentiated into neurons by simple neuronal induction protocol.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of a unique population within the UCB MSCs that is capable of instantaneous neuronal transdifferentiation and has the potential to generate neurons with the desired neuronal markers.
the characterization of the UCB-derived MSC population that is responsible for the instantaneous neurogenic potential.
the identification of unique population of pluripotent MSCs in UCB and their potential for neuronal differentiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the UCB-MScs consist of a unique heterogeneous population of progenitors that co-express MSC and neuronal markers and are capable of generating neurons with simple neuronal induction conditions or with extensive exposure to a cocktail of growth factors in stepwise protocol.
the UCB-MCSCs contain two distinct populations of progenitors with different neurogenic potentials.
the UCB-MC contains two different populations of cells with distinct neuronal differentiation potential.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified two different types of progenitors in the human UCB-derived MSC population.
the UCB-MC-derived MSCs consist of two different populations of cells with different neurogenic potentials.
UCB-MSC contains a unique population of MSCs with pluripotent stemness and neuronal potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MSCs derived from the UCB consist of a unique and heterogeneous population of progenitors with the ability to differentiate into multiple cell lineages, including neurons.
the UCB-derived MSC population consists of a heterogeneous population with multiple progenitors with varying degrees of neurogenic potential.
there is a unique population of pluripotent progenitor cells that express both MSC and neural progenitor markers, and these cells have the ability to differentiate into neurons without any induction.
